answer: I would like to talk about a friend whose energy honestly puts me to shame. The hardest-working person I know is a close friend who is building his own small business from scratch. He runs a little café near the college in Sirajganj, which he opened about two years ago with his savings and a small loan. His work ethic is genuinely [[relentless]]; he is often up before dawn and still working late into the night. As for how he shows it, what impresses me is that he never seems to cut corners, no matter how [[exhausted]] he is. He handles everything himself in these early stages, from serving customers to doing the accounts, and he does it all with a smile. He even cleans the café himself at night so that he does not have to hire extra staff yet. I think what drives him is a deep sense of [[determination]] to build something of his own rather than work for someone else. There have been moments when I worried he was pushing himself too hard, especially when he stopped seeing friends for months, but his energy is remarkable. Watching his effort slowly pay off has been genuinely [[inspiring]] to witness, and the café is now busy most evenings. As for how I feel about him, I am enormously proud of him. Honestly, he has completely changed my idea of what commitment looks like, and he reminds me that success is usually far less glamorous than people imagine.

followUps.q: Do you consider yourself a hard-working person?
followUps.answer: Fairly, yes, although not to his extreme. I work long hours during application season, but I also try to protect my evenings, because I think rest is essential if you want to [[sustain]] your effort.

followUps.q: Do you think hard work always leads to success?
followUps.answer: Not always. Hard work is essential, but luck, timing and opportunities matter too. Still, people who work consistently hard give themselves a much better chance than those who do not.

note: Added what his business is (a café in Sirajganj), concrete examples of his hard work, my worry about him and a clear 'how I feel' section.
